scientific_question: Why did stage64 produce only 0.01129 CE improvement over stage32 despite 1.44x current-Muon and 1.52x held-out phase recovery: are the additional Frobenius-recovered directions inactive under post-GELU residual-output and task-loss metrics, or are they functionally useful but lost because the tangent is refreshed too slowly?

nested_candidates.connectivity: select one 64-stage task-matched hidden-channel sequence from the exact current coherent Muon direction; stage32 is its first 32 stages
nested_candidates.angles: closed-form diagonal tangent metric using only the exact current requested Muon update

functional_metrics.post_gelu_residual_output: for activation rows H and weight update D, compare H D^T on two disjoint fixed validation windows
functional_metrics.recorded_training_gradient: exact clipped gradient from the same pre-step training batch
functional_metrics.validation_gradient: c_proj gradients on disjoint fixed validation windows
functional_metrics.finite_step_ce: simultaneously perturb the five registered c_proj layers by each actual scheduled update, evaluate the identical tokens, then exactly restore all weights

decision_rule.functional_gain_present_test_temporal_re: stage64/stage32 post-GELU current-output fixed-scale recovery >=1.25, recorded-training-gradient predicted CE decrease >=1.15x, and stage64 has lower fixed-batch CE in at least 6 of 8 phase/window comparisons
decision_rule.reject_frobenius_stage_depth_functional_: post-GELU recovery ratio <1.20, task-descent ratio <1.05, or stage64 wins no more than 2 of 8 finite-step comparisons
decision_rule.otherwise: mixed functional signal; do not promote training

execution_policy.mode: direct foreground execution and polling to exit

authorization.authorized: implement, test, and run this no-training diagnostic once
